standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter characterization of quasi-affine morphisms by being a quasi-compact open subscheme of the relative spectrum of a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras
standard_prerequisites.use: Represents the preimage under the second morphism inside a relative spectrum, which is the object that is then pushed forward.

standard_prerequisites.name: The pushforward of a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras along a quasi-compact open immersion is quasi-coherent and pulls back to the original, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the sheaf of algebras on the affine scheme V whose relative spectrum makes the square a fibre square.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relative spectrum of a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras, its compatibility with base change by an open immersion, and the fact that relative spectra over affine bases are affine
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the open immersion j into a fibre square with an affine upper right corner, giving the affine scheme in which the double preimage sits as a quasi-compact open subscheme.

core_obligations: Start with affine open U of the target and use quasi-affineness of the second morphism to write its preimage in Y as a quasi-compact open subscheme of a relative spectrum, witnessed by a quasi-compact open immersion into an affine scheme V (proof lines 2502-2507).
Represent the preimage under the first morphism inside a relative spectrum over the preimage in Y, using the same-chapter characterization applied to the first morphism (proof lines 2506-2509).

Push the sheaf of algebras forward along the open immersion into V, so that the relative spectrum over V restricts back to the relative spectrum over the open subscheme; the resulting commutative diagram has a fibre square with an affine upper right corner (proof lines 2510-2521).

Conclude that the preimage of the affine open under the composite is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme, hence quasi-affine, and therefore the composite is quasi-affine (proof lines 2521-2531).
proof_roadmap: Write the preimage under g inside a relative spectrum and then the further preimage under f inside a relative spectrum over it (proof lines 2502-2509).
Push the sheaf of algebras along the witnessing open immersion to obtain a fibre square with affine upper right corner and read off quasi-affineness (proof lines 2510-2531).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the composite of two quasi-affine morphisms is quasi-affine (statement lines 2497-2500). The counted proof is short but not a citation: it represents the preimage under the second morphism as a quasi-compact open subscheme of a relative spectrum, then represents the further preimage under the first morphism inside a relative spectrum over that, pushes the sheaf of algebras forward along the witnessing open immersion, and reads the resulting fibre square with affine upper right corner as the required presentation of the preimage of an affine open under the composite (proof lines 2502-2531). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the relative spectrum formalism and quasi-coherence of pushforwards.

This is the quasi-affine analogue of the lane's card S13-morph-composition-affine (statement 1969-1972 in old coordinates, proof 1974-1979), which is the much easier statement that the composite of affine morphisms is affine; the two have different hypotheses and conclusions, and the affine case is not used in this proof. The cited characterization lemma around 2440-2470 is an input and is not counted here.

Assumption difference with S13-morph-composition-affine: that card assumes both morphisms affine, this card assumes them quasi-affine. Conclusion difference: the conclusion here is quasi-affineness of the composite, obtained through relative spectra, whereas the affine case follows directly from the preimage criterion; neither statement implies the other as a counting object.
